entries.status: No EU-level schedule or class. EU legislation does not establish classes of narcotic or psychotropic substances; Member States classify drugs according to the 1961, 1971 and 1988 UN Conventions. The Framework Decision on illicit drug trafficking defines 'drug' as any substance covered by the 1961 Single Convention (as amended by the 1972 Protocol) or by the 1971 Convention, or listed in its Annex.

entries.checked_by: AI reader W2 (two WebFetch readings compared by script)
entries.note: Two full readings and two targeted look-ups found no entry naming it. By the item's own chemical name (5-methoxy-N,N-dimethyltryptamine) it would read as a derivative of DMT under Note 6, but the list itself does not say so. List I also has «5-Гидрокси-N-метилтриптамин и его производные...». Note 6 of the Perechen defines derivatives as substances not listed on their own (in the Perechen or the State Register of Medicines) whose structure is formed by «заменой (формальным замещением) одного или нескольких атомов водорода, галогенов и (или) гидроксильных групп» with other atoms or substituents (not hydroxyl or carboxyl groups), the substituents together having no more carbon atoms than the parent; if several parents fit, the one needing the fewest substituents decides.

Searched: DDB Updated Lists as of 20 July 2026 in full, every part read twice: precursor Tables I (27 rows) and II (8); 1961 Convention Schedule 1 (nos. 1-138), II (1-10), III (1-8 preparations), IV (1-18); 1971 Convention Schedule 1 (35 rows), II (64 rows), III (1-9), IV (1-69); and the PHILIPPINE SCHEDULE part (10 "DDB Regulations" and 7 "Board issuances"); also RA 9165 Sec. 3 definitions.
